comparison: Both evaluations support the finding of reduced Ca2+ currents in RIM-BP2 KO (C4, C33, C34, C107). OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis (p=0.0248, n=8-9), while peer reviewers describe it as 'compelling evidence' and 'high quality work' demonstrating reduced calcium channel abundance.

Both evaluations support the STED microscopy findings showing reduced Cav2.1 intensity (C7, C86, C87, C93, C96, C108). OpenEval notes the ~22% reduction (p=0.0286) with appropriate caveats about nonlinear STED measurements, while peer reviewers confirm the 'slight decrease in cluster intensity (~20%)' and accept it as supporting the electrophysiological data.

Both evaluations address minor effects on RRP measured by capacitance (C35, C49). OpenEval emphasizes the technical limitations of capacitance measurements with appropriate caveats (C61, C62), while peer reviewers accept the findings noting 'no impacts on Ca-induced exocytosis and RRP' and that 'the effects are relatively small.'

Both evaluations address non-significant findings for Cav2.2 and Munc13-1 (C90, C91, C113). OpenEval supports the findings with appropriate statistical reporting (p=0.3143, p=0.0831) and acknowledges limitations, while peer reviewers accept these results as part of the overall minor effects observed.

Both evaluations support the finding that elevated external Ca2+ can partially compensate for the KO deficit (C6, C39, C40, C42). OpenEval provides detailed statistical support (p=0.57 from mixed model), while peer reviewers note the authors 'can restore release by increasing Ca2+ influx' and accept this as evidence for reduced Ca2+ influx as a primary mechanism.

Both evaluations support the finding of unchanged coupling distance (C55, C59, C60, C122, C123). OpenEval notes similar EGTA sensitivity when Ca2+ currents are matched and acknowledges STED spatial resolution limitations, while peer reviewers accept this finding without challenge, implicitly agreeing that decoupling was not observed.

Both evaluations support the STED microscopy measurements showing no significant difference in channel-vesicle coupling distance (C94, C95). OpenEval notes consistency with EGTA sensitivity data while acknowledging spatial resolution limitations, and peer reviewers accept this finding as part of the evidence that RIM-BP2 functions differently at mossy fiber synapses.

Both evaluations support the main conclusions integrating electrophysiological and imaging data (C5, C8, C96, C119, C125). OpenEval finds the conclusion well-supported by converging evidence from multiple approaches, while peer reviewers describe it as 'compelling evidence' and 'an important contribution,' though one notes the phenotype is 'not new' compared to other systems.

Major disagreement on impaired fusion competence. OpenEval supports the claim that fusion competence is impaired beyond reduced Ca2+ influx (C65-C69, C118), citing data showing WT EPSCs remain larger than KO even when Ca2+ influx is matched. However, Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly questions this interpretation, stating the authors 'propose an altered fusion competence of the SVs, which is not so strongly supported by the data.'

Both evaluations support the comparison with previous work at different synapse types (C109, C110, C126). OpenEval finds the comparison valid and highlights synapse-specific differences, while Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly acknowledges the phenotype is 'not new' compared to hair cell active zones and that diverse RIM-BP2 functions at different synapses have been previously proposed.

OpenEval supports the finding that WT can reproduce the KO phenotype by adjusting external Ca2+ (C43-C46, p=0.88 from mixed model), providing evidence that reduced Ca2+ influx is the primary mechanism. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this is implicitly accepted as part of the overall compensation findings.

OpenEval supports the train stimulation data showing different facilitation patterns between WT and KO (C73-C81, p<0.01 from ANOVA), with differences diminishing during the train. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for these detailed train stimulation findings.

OpenEval supports the authors' acknowledgment of a major limitation regarding potential developmental compensation in the constitutive knockout (C138, C139), noting this affects interpretation of all results. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found addressing this limitation.

OpenEval supports the finding of similar paired-pulse ratios across conditions (C70-C72) with appropriately cautious interpretation based on multiple mechanisms underlying paired-pulse facilitation. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for this finding.

OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN the discrepancy with previous work regarding Munc13-1 (C111-C116), noting that while plausible explanations are provided, they remain speculative. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found addressing this discrepancy, though peer reviewers accept the non-significant Munc13-1 finding.
